questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Sam counts votes for favourite fruit with tally marks. The mangoes have 2 groups of five and 3 extra marks. How many votes did the mangoes get?
questions.explanation: Two groups of five make 10. Add the 3 extra marks to get 13.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Lily asks 10 friends to pick a favourite Australian animal. Kangaroo got 4 votes, koala 3, wombat 2 and emu 1. Which animal got the most votes?
questions.explanation: Kangaroo got 4 votes. That is more than any other animal.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Ben counts cars outside the school gate. He sees 6 red, 4 white, 5 blue and 2 black cars. How many cars did he count altogether?

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Zoe wants to sort her class into categories, like colours. Which question gives answers she can sort into categories?
choices: How many books did you read?
How many pets do you have?
How many teeth have you lost?
questions.explanation: Colours can be sorted into groups like red, blue and green. The other questions give counted numbers.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Votes for ice cream flavours were: chocolate 8, vanilla 5, strawberry 3. Jess draws a bar graph of the votes. Which flavour has the tallest bar?
questions.explanation: The tallest bar shows the most votes. Chocolate has 8 votes, the most.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: In a picture graph, one gum leaf stands for 2 children. Room 4 has 5 gum leaves. How many children does Room 4 have?
questions.explanation: Each leaf is worth 2 children. Count by twos five times: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Rainy days in four months were: June 9, July 12, August 7, September 5. Which two months together had 16 rainy days?
questions.explanation: June and August make 9 + 7 = 16. The other pairs add to different numbers.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Group A spins a spinner 20 times and gets red 12 times. Group B uses the same spinner and gets red 9 times. What does this show?
choices: Group B spun the spinner wrongly
Results can be different each time we try
questions.explanation: Chance results change from one try to the next, even with the same spinner.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A bag has only red counters. Mia picks one without looking. How likely is it that the counter is red?
questions.explanation: Every counter in the bag is red, so it must be red. That is certain.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A bag has 9 blue marbles and 1 yellow marble. Sam picks one without looking. How likely is a yellow marble?
questions.explanation: Only 1 of the 10 marbles is yellow. It can happen, but it probably will not.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: It is impossible to roll a 7 with one normal dice numbered 1 to 6.
questions.explanation: The dice only has the numbers 1 to 6, so a 7 can never happen.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Mia has 1 ticket in a raffle of 100 tickets. She says winning is unlikely. Which reason is best?
choices: She has only a tiny share of all the tickets
questions.explanation: She holds 1 ticket out of 100, so most of the time another ticket will win.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Ali tosses a coin 10 times and gets 6 heads. He tosses it 10 more times. What will probably happen?
choices: He will get exactly 6 heads again
He might get a different number of heads
questions.explanation: Each set of tosses can turn out differently. The number of heads may change.

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A class rolls a dice 20 times. They get 4 five times, 5 four times and 6 two times. How many rolls gave a 4 or more?
questions.explanation: Add the rolls of 4, 5 and 6 together: 5 + 4 + 2 = 11.
